newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp sees tough appliance market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp sees tough appliance market.

text.p: Wine packaging group Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Monday it sees the Australian market for appliances remaining competitive, but forecast a possible upturn in the housing sector in early 1997.

"The market environment is likely to remain fairly competitive but we do see prospects of a housing upturn as early as 1997, perhaps a bit earlier with the recent interest rate cut," Southcorp managing director Graham Kraehe said.
"But we are planning on a difficult and competitive market environment as we go forward."

Earlier, Southcorp posted a 2.5 percent rise in net profit before abnormals to A$118.2 million for the year to June 30. The group booked abnormal and extraordinary gains after tax of A$6 million, lifting the bottom line to A$124.2 million.

Earnings grew in all the group's major divisions -- wine, packaging and home appliances -- despite a US$2.5 million loss in its U.S. water heater business, which suffered from continued price volatility, Kraehe told reporters in Melbourne.
The packaging business grew despite a flat local economy and a wet summer which dampened beverage consumption, Kraehe said.

The group's packaging division will focus on innovation in the high-growth PET (polyethylene terephthalate) plastic packaging business, he said. "We are starting to see some beer being packaged in PET," Kraehe added.
Asia will become increasingly important to the packaging business with "continuing strong demand in that market", he said.
Southcorp shares were four cents firmer at A$3.22 at 3.50 p.m. (0550 GMT) -- Melbourne bureau 613-9286-1421
